info: In Portuguese, states and conditions are often expressed using "ser" (to be) for permanent characteristics or inherent qualities, and "estar" (to be) for temporary states or conditions. For example, Está quente ("It is hot") describes a temporary weather condition, while Ele é corajoso ("He is brave") reflects a permanent quality. Personal conditions like hunger or thirst use "ter" (to have) or "estar com", e.g., Tenho fome or Estou com fome ("I am hungry," literally "I have hunger" or "I am with hunger"). This flexibility allows Portuguese to express both the nature and context of various states.
